summary:
Voters in Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin a process towards independence from Canada. With more than 1 million votes counted, about 76% backed remaining in Canada, while 23% supported beginning a process that could lead to separation. The result is a victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity, and separatists say they will pursue a second referendum.

Houthi forces struck a military camp in government-controlled Shabwa province with three ballistic missiles, killing at least 50 people, local authorities said. Officials said the camp was being used as a training centre for new recruits, and the Iran-backed group has claimed responsibility. The attack appeared to be among the deadliest of the renewed war.

France has imposed curfews in parts of Paris and other cities after nationwide rioting. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez acknowledged that police were underprepared for the scale of the riots. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu defended police efforts and pledged to restore order.

headlines.title: Alberta voters reject starting a process to leave Canada
headlines.summary: About 76% of Alberta voters backed remaining in Canada, while 23% supported beginning a process that could lead to separation, with more than 1 million votes counted. Separatists say they will pursue a second referendum.

headlines.title: Houthi missile strike kills at least 50 recruits in Yemen
headlines.summary: Three missiles hit a camp in government-controlled Shabwa province that officials said was a training centre for new recruits. The Iran-backed Houthis have claimed responsibility for the attack, which local authorities said killed at least 50 people.

headlines.title: France imposes curfews in Paris and other cities after rioting
headlines.summary: Curfews were imposed in parts of Paris and other cities after nationwide rioting. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez acknowledged police were underprepared, and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu pledged to restore order.

headlines.title: Floods in eastern Spain kill at least four people
headlines.summary: Torrential rain battered Spain's eastern Mediterranean coast, sweeping away cars and submerging roads. Emergency crews carried out more than 400 rescues in Valencia, where rainfall reached 700 litres per square metre.

headlines.title: Zelensky accuses US of delaying Patriot missile deliveries
headlines.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused the United States of holding up Patriot interceptor missiles already paid for by European allies. The accusation came as tensions with the Trump administration deepened over military aid and intelligence sharing.

headlines.title: Trump says he is open to three-way meeting with Xi and Putin
headlines.summary: Trump said he was open to a three-way meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin during his visit to China next month, with nuclear weapons on the agenda. Putin has floated a summit with Trump and Xi on a Ukraine deal, from which Zelensky would be excluded.

headlines.title: UN food programme cuts aid to 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza
headlines.summary: The World Food Programme said funding shortages forced it to end support for more than half a million Palestinians in Gaza. Two-thirds of Gaza's population faces crisis levels of food insecurity, and 200,000 people are in danger of famine.

headlines.title: Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie found guilty of 191 murders
headlines.summary: A Kenyan court found Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of 190 children and one adult. Prosecutors said Mackenzie had ordered followers to starve themselves and their children.
